title: Project Coordinator
description:
--- Role Overview

The Project Coordinator owns the operational backbone of renovation projects from pre-kickoff through close-out. Where the Project Manager owns scope, budget, and the client relationship, you own the systems, documentation, schedule tracking, and vendor follow-through that keep every project moving.

This is an ownership role, not a task-taking role. You are expected to spot slippage before your PM does, chase answers without being reminded, and bring your PM a recommendation rather than a question. You will typically support two to four active projects at a time and maintain daily contact with contractors, subcontractors, and vendors to verify site activity, confirm schedule adherence, and document progress.



--- Key Responsibilities

** Project Systems & Documentation

1. Own project folder structure, Slack channels, and document filing so that links, drive folders, and templates are correctly filed and accessible without prompting.

2. Maintain project trackers and proposal decks as the single source of truth, updated from Matterport scans, floorplans, and vendor bids within 24 hours of new information.

3. Build and update backyard overlays and other visual documentation using survey data, drone photos, and site imagery.

4. Keep Buildertrend and all other project systems current. You are accountable for data integrity, not just data entry.



** Schedule & Site Accountability

1. Maintain daily communication with contractors and subcontractors to confirm on-site presence and active work at assigned projects.

2. Obtain photographic progress documentation no fewer than three (3) times per week, ensuring images are clear, time-stamped, and tied to specific milestones or ongoing construction activity.

3. Compare actual site progress against the baseline schedule and flag variance early, before it becomes a client-visible delay.

4. Escalate delays, missed updates, or contractor no-shows to the Project Manager within 24 hours, paired with a proposed recovery option.



** Vendor & Permitting Support

1. Run bid requests end-to-end: issue, track, chase, and close out estimates and compliance documents (W9s, COIs, licenses).

2. Prepare permit application packets to local requirements and submit to the appropriate portals or hand off to the permitting team as a complete package that requires no rework.

3. Submit vendor payment requests using the designated SOP.

Validate invoices and submit to Buildertrend.

4. Maintain vendor records and flag lapsed insurance or licensing before it blocks work on site.



** Client & Stakeholder Communication

1. Draft client recaps, kickoff materials, and bi-weekly updates by compiling inputs from the PM and vendor check-ins.

2. Monitor project Slack channels and surface urgent messages or requests to the PM with the context needed to act.

3. Schedule internal and client-facing meetings, including kickoff and proposal calls.



** Construction & Close-Out

1. Own punch list tracking from creation through sign-off and confirm completion with photo evidence.

2. Coordinate final photography, walkthrough scheduling, and close-out document packaging.

3. Collect final invoices from all contractors and audit each contract to verify that all agreed-upon work has been completed.

4. Support quality control from project initiation through close-out, ensuring all work meets established standards and specifications.



--- What Success Looks Like

- Day 30: Fully independent on project systems, trackers, and filing across all assigned projects.

- Day 60: Running vendor follow-up and permit packet preparation without PM prompting, with zero missed photo documentation cycles.

- Day 90: Your PM comes to you for project status rather than assembling it themselves. Punch lists and close-out packages are complete and audit-ready.



????‍???? Skills & Qualifications

** Required

- 2+ years in project coordination, operations, or administrative support in a fast-moving environment.

- Demonstrated follow-through. You close loops without being chased.

- Strong written English: clear, professional, and concise.

- Advanced Google Workspace skills, particularly Sheets (filters, lookups, conditional formatting).

- Comfort managing three or more concurrent projects with competing deadlines.

- Availability during US business hours, with reliable high-speed internet and a quiet workspace for calls.



** Preferred

- Experience with Buildertrend, Slack, ClickUp, Asana, or comparable project management tooling.

- Background in construction, renovation, design, real estate, or property operations.

- Exposure to permitting, inspections, or municipal processes.



--- This Role Is Not a Fit If

- You need step-by-step direction to make progress.

- You go quiet when you hit a blocker instead of escalating it.

- You are looking for a purely administrative, ticket-taking role.

title: Bookkeeping / Accounting / Admin support
description:
We're looking for an experienced bookkeeper to lead a conversion project for a project-based service client, moving them from cash-basis QuickBooks Online with minimal job tracking to a full accrual-basis system with detailed job costing.



This is hands-on, technically demanding work. You'll be building the structure, not just maintaining it — so we're looking for someone who understands why accrual accounting and job costing matter, not just how to enter transactions.



What You'll Be Doing

Converting the client from cash to accrual basis in QuickBooks Online.

Setting up Customers and Projects in QBO to track revenue and costs by individual job (and, where practical, by sub-unit within a job).

Separating revenue and direct costs by type and coding each transaction to the correct Project.

Tracking balance sheet items separately, including customer deposits, unbilled revenue, billings in excess of costs, retainage, and work-in-progress (WIP).

Implementing progress invoicing for long-duration jobs, while recognizing revenue based on percentage-of-completion, not simply the amount invoiced.

Maintaining a monthly WIP schedule outside of QBO to calculate percentage-of-completion, and posting the corresponding month-end adjusting journal entries into QBO.

Reconciling the WIP schedule to the general ledger each month and flagging discrepancies.



The end goal: give the client real, accurate visibility into job-level profitability and overall financial position — revenue and costs reflected when the work is actually performed, not just when cash or invoices move.



What We're Looking For

Solid, demonstrated experience with QuickBooks Online, including Projects/job costing features.

Real working knowledge of accrual accounting principles, not just cash-basis bookkeeping.

Familiarity with percentage-of-completion / WIP accounting — ideally you've built or maintained a WIP schedule before, even informally.

Comfort working with retainage, billings in excess of costs, and unbilled revenue as distinct balance sheet items.

Strong attention to detail — this build sets the foundation the client will rely on going forward.

Ability to work independently, communicate clearly in writing, and flag issues proactively rather than waiting to be asked.

title: Creative Project Manager & Design Operations Specialist
description:
Role overview: 

You are the operational backbone of a small creative studio. You own client communication, project flow, and quality control, and you execute design work directly when the primary designer is unavailable. The founder’s name is on every deliverable. Your job is to make sure nothing leaves the studio that the founder would not proudly sign.



Client Communication & Proactive Reporting

• Acknowledge every client request quickly with a clear, realistic timeline

• Send status updates on a set cadence (Mon/Wed/Fri minimum) without being asked

• When a client sends assets, materials, or information, notify the founder same day with what arrived, what it is for, and the deadline

• Update clients proactively when timelines shift, manage urgency without letting everything become urgent



Project Management

• Translate requests into fully scoped ClickUp tasks: complete instructions, correct files and Drive links, client history, due dates matching commitments

• Route work to the primary designer first, take on execution when they are at capacity

• Schedule against real capacity, flag conflicts early with proposed solutions

Design QA (Non-Negotiable)

• Every deliverable is verified before it ships: kerning, spacing, alignment, weight consistency, resolution, export quality, copy accuracy

• When modifying existing brand assets, work from and verify against the source file. Never repurpose an old asset as new work

• A 5-minute edit gets the same precision as a full project



Direct Design Execution

• The primary designer works async off-hours. When time-sensitive requests land, you execute them yourself to full professional standard: logo lockups, typography adjustments, layout corrections, production edits

• If a request exceeds your skill level, say so immediately and set expectations. Never attempt-and-ship



Admin & Organization

• Draft scopes of work from provided formulas, track approvals, send W-9s and documents

• Maintain clean Drive structure and naming conventions

Tools: ClickUp, Google Drive, Figma, Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign, Canva, 
. Working familiarity with Shopify, Webflow, WordPress, Squarespace, Wix.





Required skills

• Proven production design ability with a portfolio showing typography and logo lockup work

• Trained design eye, spots kerning and weight issues without being told

• Track record managing clients and projects for a small team or agency

• Proactive reporting habits, demonstrated, not claimed

• Honest self-assessment of skill limits

Nice-to-have: packaging or print design, experience supporting a creative founder or studio, retainer vs project familiarity

title: VIDEO EDITOR, SHORT-FORM REELS (Remote · PHP & SA)
description:
WHO WE ARE

We're a small creator-management agency (Portugal HQ) that builds handmade brands for a tiny roster of creators. The founder works on every account. We're hiring our first dedicated editor for one flagship creator: a cozy homemaker lifestyle brand (warm home, garden, cooking, comfort) with a retro-gaming thread woven through it.





WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY EDIT

Instagram Reels (15 to 30s) for a warm domestic-lifestyle brand. Think lamp-lit rooms, cooking and garden moments, soft-spoken voiceover, a retro game paused on the TV in the background. Warm and cozy, but never slow or boring. Our editing style:



- 2-3s pacing rule - Something must happen every 2 to 3 seconds: a sound effect, a subtle zoom, a cut, a text pop, an on-screen detail. Micro-events keep retention high. The trick is doing this while the reel still FEELS calm and warm, not chaotic. Gentle movement, not zoom-punch spam.

- Optimal trimming - Tight cuts, no dead air, no wasted frames. Every clip trimmed to its best moment.

- Sound design as a core skill - Domestic texture (kettle, chopping, rain on the window, keyboard clicks) layered with retro game SFX accents and a whisper-register voice. You'll integrate sound effects constantly. Our audience recognizes the brand by sound in 3 seconds.

- Simple, clean transitions and effects - Smooth and purposeful. No flashy transition packs, no trend-chasing effects that fight the cozy vibe.

- Nostalgia-literate accents - You don't need to be a Nintendo expert. You'll work from our reference bank of era-correct sounds and visuals, and you'll learn why a 1998 chest-opening sound outperforms any trending audio for our audience.



You'll get a full style bible, hook templates, banned-elements list, and direct feedback from the founder. We want an editor who becomes THE voice of this brand's edit, not a gig-worker juggling 30 clients.





WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU

- Some experience with short-form vertical content (Reels, Shorts, TikTok). Show us, don't tell us.

- Strong pacing instincts: you know how to keep a reel alive every 2 to 3 seconds without making it feel loud

- Clean audio mixing and confident sound-effect work. This brand lives and dies on sound.

- Solid color grading fundamentals (warm grades, skin tones)

- CapCut, Premiere Pro, or DaVinci Resolve all welcome. We judge the output, not the software.

- A good laptop that can handle raw vertical footage and deliver on deadline

- Fluent written English. Feedback loops are async and fast.

- Reliable internet



Bonus points: you've edited cozy-lifestyle, cooking, home, or ASMR-adjacent content · you understand parasocial audiences · you grew up on PlayStation, Nintendo, or Sega · you've worked with creator brands before.

title: Creative Marketing Lead – Brand & Campaign Design | Full-Time | Remote
description:
Creative Marketing Lead – Brand & Campaign Design | Full-Time | Remote

Location: Remote, Philippines-based preferred

Schedule: Full-Time

Work Hours: U.S. business hours

Compensation: $7–$9 USD/hour based on experience and portfolio

Type: Long-Term | Full-Time



About the Role

We're looking for a Creative Marketing Lead to own creative production and direction across our marketing efforts — not just executing what's handed to you, but shaping how campaigns look, feel, and come together. This role is for someone with strong design instincts, real ownership of brand identity work, and the judgment to make creative calls with minimal hand-holding. You'll be the go-to person for creative output: setting the standard, keeping quality and consistency high, and — as the team grows — guiding other designers or freelancers on projects you lead.



This isn't a pure production role. We want someone who can take a rough idea or a marketing goal and turn it into a finished, on-brand campaign — and who's comfortable being the person who says "here's the better way to do this."



What You'll Do

Creative Direction & Production

Own the creative execution of marketing campaigns from concept to finished asset — social,
, web, ads, presentations, event materials

Set and maintain visual/brand standards across all creative output

Make creative decisions independently once given a goal or brief, rather than waiting for detailed direction

Build and evolve brand guidelines, templates, and systems that keep future production fast and consistent

Adapt and extend existing designs across formats without losing brand integrity



Leadership & Collaboration

Act as the point person for creative quality — review work (your own and, over time, any contributors' or freelancers' work) before it goes out

Translate marketing goals into a creative plan, then delegate or execute accordingly

Communicate proactively on status, blockers, and creative recommendations rather than just waiting for feedback

Partner directly with the marketing/leadership team on campaign strategy from the creative side



Project & Systems Ownership

Track and prioritize creative requests and deadlines across multiple concurrent projects

Keep design files, templates, and brand assets organized and easy for the team to use

Build repeatable systems/processes that reduce turnaround time as volume grows



Required Experience



Proven experience owning creative output for a brand or agency — not just producing individual assets, but shaping how they look and work together

Demonstrated experience building brand identity/guidelines from scratch (not only working from existing brand kits)

Strong eye for layout, typography, branding, and visual consistency

Fluency with: Figma, Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign), Canva

Comfortable using AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or similar) as part of the creative workflow

Experience managing or mentoring other designers, or clearly demonstrated readiness to (e.g., led QA/review of others' work, ran a small design team, trained others)

Strong written and spoken English

Highly organized, deadline-driven, comfortable managing multiple projects at once

Comfortable working remotely with a U.S.-based team, full graveyard/US-hours overlap



What Success Looks Like

Creative output is consistently on-brand, polished, and requires minimal revision cycles

You're proactively flagging better creative approaches, not just executing requests as given

Templates, systems, and brand assets are organized and scalable

The team trusts you to make creative calls without close supervision

As the team grows, you're able to review and guide other designers' work



To Apply

Please submit:

1. A viewable link to your updated resume

2. A portfolio showing brand identity/guideline work you built from scratch (not just individual asset production) — plus social,
, web, and campaign samples

3. A short paragraph on: a project where you led creative direction (not just execution), and any experience reviewing or guiding other designers' work

4. A list of design, project management, and AI tools you use

title: Project Coordinator; Client Experience
description:
--- Role Overview

This is a Project Coordinator role with a client-facing specialization. You carry the same project coordination responsibilities as the rest of the PC team, and you additionally serve as the communication and calendaring backbone for our Head of Construction by:

 - Monitoring client communications and updates

 - Coordinating kickoff meetings and as needed client meetings with the Head of Construction

 - Client correspondence, and the follow-up loop that keeps clients informed and internal commitments visible



Expect roughly 60% core project coordination and 40% client communications and calendaring, though the mix will flex with project load. This role will be client facing, so the bar on writing quality and responsiveness is high.



--- Key Responsibilities

** Client Communications (Specialization)

1. Draft, edit, and send client-facing correspondence, including recaps, kickoff summaries, proposal follow-ups, and bi-weekly progress updates, in TCC's voice and to a standard that requires minimal editing.

2. Serve as first-line responder on client
, using AI tools to triage by urgency, route what needs leadership attention, and handle what you can on behalf of the Head of Construction.

3. Track every client commitment made on calls and in writing, and confirm each one is closed.

4. Prepare pre-call briefs covering agenda, open items, prior commitments, and current project status.

5. Send post-call recaps within one business day, with clear owners and dates on every action item.



** Kick-off Calendaring & Executive Support

- Own management of the Head of Construction’s calendar: schedule, reschedule, protect focus blocks, moving things around to fit in short pop-up meetings, and resolve conflicts across time zones.

- Coordinate client-facing meetings end-to-end, including invites, agendas, conference links, reminders, and materials prepared in advance.

- Capture meeting notes and action items from recorded calls and convert them into tracked follow-ups.

- Anticipate scheduling friction and resolve it before it reaches staff.

- Prepare project markup and pricing based on client intake forms, ensuring accuracy and healthy margins

- Review intake form details closely to translate raw project scope into finalized cost and pricing structure

- Flag pricing or scope discrepancies to the Director of Construction before finalizing markup

- Support margin optimization by applying consistent pricing logic across projects

- Coordinate with the design team to have backyard/outdoor renderings finalized before client kickoff calls



** Project Coordination (Shared with the PC Team)

- Organize and maintain project folders, Slack channels, trackers, and proposal decks, keeping all information current and accessible.

- Maintain daily communication with contractors and subcontractors to confirm on-site presence and ongoing work.

- Obtain photographic progress documentation no fewer than three (3) times per week, clear and time-stamped.

- Escalate delays, missed updates, or contractor no-shows to the Project Manager within 24 hours.

- Track bid requests and follow up with vendors to collect required estimates and compliance documents (W9s, COIs).

- Assist with permit application packets and submit vendor payment requests per SOP.

- Maintain punch list tracking and support close-out documentation, final photography, and walkthrough scheduling.



--- What Success Looks Like

- Day 30: Managing Fordham's calendar independently, with no double-bookings and no client meeting scheduled without materials ready.

- Day 60: Client correspondence going out with light review only. No client commitment is dropped or untracked.

- Day 90: Clients experience TCC as consistently responsive, and Fordham's time is spent on client conversations rather than coordinating them.



--- Skills & Qualifications



** Required

- Native-level or near-native written English. This role writes directly to clients.

- Excellent spoken English and comfort on client-facing calls.

- 2+ years in client communications, executive assistance, account coordination, or a similar client-facing role.

- Proven calendar management across US time zones, including for a senior stakeholder.

- Strong judgment on what to escalate, what to route, and what to handle independently.

- Discretion with sensitive client, project, and financial information.

- Advanced Google Workspace skills, especially Calendar, Gmail, Docs, and Sheets.

title: Shopify E-Commerce Operations & CRO Manager
description:
LIV BODY is a U.S.-based health and wellness brand looking for an experienced Shopify E-Commerce Operations & CRO Manager to take ownership of our website operations, promotional launches, QA, conversion optimization, and ongoing site improvements.



This is NOT a basic Shopify product-upload or page-building role.



We are looking for someone who understands how a growing e-commerce brand operates and can independently take a promotion from brief to launch, make sure every component works correctly, identify problems before customers do, and continually improve the shopping experience.



Responsibilities:



• Own day-to-day Shopify website operations and maintenance

• Build and QA promotional campaigns, discount structures, bundles, offers, landing pages, and product page updates

• Thoroughly test promotions before launch across desktop and mobile

• Troubleshoot Shopify theme, app, checkout, discount, and merchandising issues

• Coordinate website changes with marketing, paid media,
/SMS, and creative teams

• Improve product pages, navigation, merchandising, upsells, and conversion paths

• Monitor the site for broken links, pricing errors, mobile issues, outdated content, and other problems

• Recommend and implement CRO improvements based on customer behavior and performance

• Manage Shopify apps and integrations and identify opportunities to improve the existing tech stack

• Maintain clear documentation and QA checklists for launches

• Communicate proactively about issues, deadlines, dependencies, and launch readiness



What we're looking for:



• Strong hands-on Shopify experience, ideally with Shopify Plus or high-volume DTC brands

• Experience managing e-commerce operations for U.S.-based brands is strongly preferred

• Demonstrated experience executing complex promotions and offers

• Strong understanding of CRO and e-commerce best practices

• Excellent QA skills and extreme attention to detail

• Ability to troubleshoot problems independently rather than waiting for step-by-step instructions

• Comfortable working with Shopify themes, apps, integrations, and basic HTML/CSS

• Strong written English and communication skills

• Reliable and able to work with deadlines and scheduled promotional launches



HOW TO APPLY:



Please follow ALL instructions below. Applications missing any requested item will not move forward.



1. Tell us briefly about your Shopify and e-commerce operations experience.



2. Send links to 2–3 LIVE Shopify stores you have personally worked on. For each store, explain specifically what you were responsible for. Please do not simply send a portfolio list.



3. Describe one complex promotion, offer, or e-commerce launch you personally implemented. Explain what you built, any challenges involved, and how you tested it before launch.



4. Share your typical pre-launch Shopify QA process. What exactly do you check before approving a promotion or site update to go live?



5. Record a NEW 3–5 minute Loom video specifically for this application. Please share your screen and walk us through a Shopify project or store you personally worked on. Show us something meaningful you built, managed, optimized, or troubleshot and explain your role.



A generic introduction video or a demonstration of basic tasks such as uploading products will not satisfy this requirement.



6. Tell us your:

   • Current location/time zone

   • Availability

   • Desired monthly rate

   • Number of hours available per week

   • Earliest possible start date



Finally, begin your application with the words “LIV BODY READY” so we know you read the entire posting.



We are looking for someone who can eventually OWN website operations, not simply complete assigned Shopify tasks. If you are proactive, highly detail-oriented, technically capable, and genuinely understand e-commerce, we'd love to hear from you.

title: INBOUND APPOINTMENT SETTER — HAIR SALON (WARM FACEBOOK/INSTAGRAM LEADS, $1,250–$2,000/MO OTE + 13TH MONTH PAY)
description:
READ THIS FIRST



We're hiring ONE full-time Inbound Appointment Setter to call warm leads from our
 and Instagram ad campaigns for a color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California.



This is NOT cold calling. Every lead you speak to has already raised their hand by submitting their info through one of our ads. Your job is to reach them fast, build trust quickly, understand what they actually want, and guide them into a booked appointment.



This role demands two things at once: sharp conversational judgment AND tight process discipline. The conversations are where you win or lose the booking. The process — cadences, call dispositions, CRM hygiene, follow-up tasks — is what makes the whole system work and what lets us measure anything. You need both. People who are great at one and sloppy at the other don't last here.



On the conversation side, what we're really hiring for is the ability to think on your feet. Someone replies three days later with just "sorry, been busy." Someone says they want highlights but describes something else entirely. Someone says "that's a bit far for me" but what they really mean is they don't see why it's worth the drive. If you can read what people actually mean and move the conversation forward without being told what to say next, you'll do well here.



If you need to be spoon-fed a script for every situation, this won't work.



THIS IS A SALES ROLE. YOU NEED AT LEAST 6 MONTHS OF EXPERIENCE

PERSUADING PEOPLE AND MOVING THEM TOWARD A BOOKED APPOINTMENT

OR A SALE.



OTE: $1,250–$2,000/month (base $900–$1,000 + uncapped performance bonuses).

13th month pay included — paid every December, on top of your base. Not baked in. Not restructured. A full extra month of base pay, added on top.



---



ABOUT THE COMPANY



You'll be employed by Midnight Siren, a growth and client acquisition company that operates and supports beauty service businesses. Your day-to-day work focuses on a family-owned, color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California that has served the Inland Empire for over 21 years.



The salon has 4.9 stars on Google with 200+ reviews and a stylist team with 75+ combined years of experience. The business is real, established, and respected in its market.



You'll work directly under Ethan, the founder of Midnight Siren — no middle managers, no agency layers between you and the person making decisions. The Midnight Siren team is small and tightly focused. The stylists at salon handle the in-salon experience; you and Ethan handle everything that gets a client booked.



A note on team structure: you will be the only appointment setter on the team. Your day-to-day working relationship is directly with Ethan. There are no peer-level coworkers, no team chat with other appointment setters, no group energy to feed off. If you thrive with autonomy, clear systems, and a direct manager relationship, this works well. If you need a team environment or peer social dynamic to stay motivated, this will feel isolating over time.



We're in an active scaling phase. Core processes exist and are being refined. They don't change daily, but they evolve as we learn. If you like improving systems alongside a team, you'll fit. If you want a fully crystallized corporate environment where nothing ever shifts, you won't.



---



WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING



This is a front-line revenue role, not customer support.



Daily:



- Call new
/Instagram ad leads within minutes of opt-in (speed matters — you'll have task notifications throughout the day)

- Run our call script for the structured parts of the call, and use our frameworks + your own judgment for discovery and objection handling. The script covers the greeting, the offer, pricing, and the booking ask. Discovery can't be fully scripted — clients say what they say, and you'll need to adapt in real time.

- Respond to inbound SMS,
 
, and Instagram DMs that get escalated to a human when our AI can't handle them

- Collect cards on file via secure link (never over the phone), book appointments, reschedule, and cancel

- Call no-shows to get them back on the calendar

- Coordinate with stylists about client requests and scheduling needs

- Create follow-up tasks in HighLevel (our CRM)

- Submit a brief end-of-day report with your numbers



Weekly:



- One coaching/review call with Ethan (~30–45 min)

- Async coaching via Loom video reviews on your live call recordings between meetings

- Review your KPIs, own your numbers, and bring data-backed ideas to improve them



During training (first 2–4 weeks):



We'll meet daily for live coaching to get you fully ramped before transitioning to the weekly + async cadence.



---



A WORD ON THE CALL SCRIPT (READ CAREFULLY)



We use a script. We also need you to think.



Where the script is fixed: the greeting, how we introduce the salon, how we present the offer, how we state pricing, the booking ask, and our core objection responses. These are tested and they work. You run them as written. Your tone, warmth, and pacing are what make them sound human — not changing the words.



Where the script can't help you: everything a real client throws at you. A vague text with no context. A client describing a service using the wrong name. Someone who's hesitant but won't say why. Someone who asks about price before you've figured out what they actually want. There is no script for these. There's a framework, and there's your judgment.



This is the part people underestimate. A big chunk of this job is not reciting — it's listening to what someone actually means and figuring out the next move in seconds, while they're on the phone with you.



Scripts do change here, but only based on data. If you bring an idea for a better line, we'll A/B test it. If it wins, it becomes the script. What we don't do is let setters freelance changes on the fly, because then we can't measure what works.



If you want to be told exactly what to say in every situation, this role will frustrate you. If you like having strong structure AND room to think, you'll do well.



---



SCHEDULE (PACIFIC TIME — GRAVEYARD SHIFT IN PHILIPPINES)



All schedule references in this post are in US Pacific Time. Because PH is 15-16 hours ahead of California, each shift starts late at night your time and ends the following morning.

- US workdays: Monday through Friday

- US days off: Saturday and Sunday

- Hours per day: 8 hours of work + 1 hour of break (30 min lunch + 2× 15 min breaks, or 30 min lunch + 1× 30 min break — your call)

- Pacific Time (US): 7:45 AM – 4:45 PM PST



Philippine Time during US Standard Time (roughly November through mid-March):



Shift runs 11:45 PM – 8:45 AM PHT

- A US Monday shift = late Monday night through Tuesday morning your time

- A US Friday shift = late Friday night through Saturday morning your time

- Your days off in PH local time: Sunday and Monday (until your shift starts late Monday night)



Philippine Time during US Daylight Savings Time (roughly mid-March through early November):



- Shift runs 10:45 PM – 7:45 AM PHT

- Same day-shift logic as above — shift starts the previous calendar evening in PH



This schedule is FIXED. It's based on data showing when our booking demand peaks. If you need flexible hours, rotating shifts, or plan to hold another job during these times, this role is not a fit.

Please re-read this section carefully and make sure BOTH the standard-time and daylight-savings schedules work for you long-term before applying. The 1-hour shift twice a year is non-negotiable — it follows US business hours. Please make sure BOTH schedules work for you long-term before applying.



---



COMPENSATION



Base pay:



$900–$1,000/month (depending on experience), paid via Wise on the 1st and 15th of every month.



13TH MONTH PAY included — paid every December on top of your regular base, not restructured into it. Prorated in your first year if you start mid-year. Total annualized base compensation including 13th month: $11,700–$13,000.



Performance bonuses (uncapped, paid monthly):



- $3 per new client showed appointment

- $2 per existing client showed appointment

- $1 per rebooking confirmation (low-effort confirmation calls for clients who already booked through the salon)



Tiered cumulative threshold bonuses (paid monthly):



- +$75 at 90 showed appointments/month

- +$150 at 120 showed appointments/month

- +$350 at 150 showed appointments/month



Worked examples:



Baseline performer — 90 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950 (midpoint)

- Performance: ~$225 (avg $2.50/show × 90)

- Threshold bonus: $75

- Total: ~$1,250/month



Solid performer — 120 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950

- Performance: ~$300 (avg $2.50/show × 120)

- Threshold bonus: $225 ($75 + $150)

- Total: ~$1,475/month



Top performer — 150 showed appointments/month (90% show rate on ~167 booked):

- Base: $1,000

- Performance: $450 ($3×90 new + $2×20 existing + $1×40 rebooking)

- Threshold bonuses: $575 ($75 + $150 + $350)

- Total: ~$2,025/month



This is a PERFORMANCE-PAY ROLE. 30–50% of your monthly income should be earned through bonuses. The base is intentionally modest. If you want a high guaranteed salary with low expectations, this is not the role.



---



OTHER BENEFITS



1. Annual performance-based raise after your first year

2. 14 days of PTO per year, single bucket, available after 90-day probation (use for vacation, holidays, sickness — your call). For planned multi-day time off, give us at least 1 week's notice so we can plan coverage. Emergencies are understood — just communicate as soon as you can.

3. 90-day initial probation period. Pay is NOT REDUCED during probation.

---



TARGET KPIs



- Lead to Booking Rate: 25%+

- Show Rate: 90%+

- Bookings per day: 4–9

- Showed appointments per month: 100–160

- Daily volume: Finish all assigned tasks each day. We supply ~17–25 leads per day plus follow-ups, no-shows, reactivations, and rebooking confirmations. HIGH CALL VOLUME (150–250 CALLS/DAY) IS NORMAL AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. If that sounds overwhelming instead of energizing, this is not a fit.



---



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



Background:



- Female candidates tend to perform best with our 35–65 female clientele, so we especially encourage strong female applicants — but the role is open to all genders.

- Bilingual (English + Spanish) is a plus but not required.



Non-negotiable skills:



The five that matter most — these are what we screen hardest for:



- Real-time thinking. You generate a good response in seconds, not minutes. Under pressure, with no script in front of you. This is the single biggest predictor of success in this role.

- Inferential listening. You hear what someone means, not just what they said. A client says "I need to talk to my husband first" — she's usually not asking for permission, she's telling you something about price or certainty that she doesn't want to say directly. If you take everything at face value, you'll lose bookings.

- Conversational initiative. You never dead-end a conversation, and you don't give up on a lead that's still alive. A client says "that's kind of far for me" — a weak setter says "no problem, thanks anyway" and loses her. What she's actually telling you is that she doesn't believe the drive is worth it yet. That's not a rejection, it's an assumption you haven't disproven. Answering someone's question is only half a response; the other half is the move that keeps things going.

- Rapport building. You can get someone to open up and feel comfortable with you fast. This is the biggest factor in whether someone books. These are emotional decisions, not logical ones. You don't need American cultural references — you need to make people feel heard, understood, and safe.

- Diagnostic reframing. You can say someone's problem back to them more clearly than they said it. When you do that, people assume you have the solution. It's the fastest way to build trust that exists.



Everything else:



- ADVANCED ENGLISH WITH MINIMAL ACCENT. An American listener should not need to strain to understand you. If we have to focus to follow what you're saying, that's a disqualifier.

- STRONG SPOKEN COMMUNICATION — CLEAR, CONFIDENT VOICE. YOU DO NOT RAMBLE. YOU ARE NOT SOFT-SPOKEN. If you fill silence with words because dead air makes you nervous, this won't work.

- Typing speed: 40 wpm minimum (60+ strongly preferred). You'll be taking notes and sending texts while talking. You'll submit a typing test screenshot with your application.

- Process discipline. Every call gets dispositioned correctly. Every lead moves through the right cadence. Every opportunity gets marked accurately in the CRM. This isn't optional admin — it's how we measure everything. Great conversations with sloppy process still means we're flying blind.

- Script discipline for the structured parts of the call.

- Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused.

- Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified.

- Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising.

- Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance.

- CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred.

- High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one.

- Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing.

- Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load.



Preferred:



- Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry

- Personal interest in beauty or self-care

- Experience working with older female clientele (35–65)

- Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster)



Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT):



We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean:



- Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout.

- Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words.

- Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat.

- Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down.

- Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses.

- KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them.



---



TECH REQUIREMENTS



Non-negotiable:



- Internet minimum requirements: 50 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Stable connection. We will test your speed and audio live from your actual work setup before we hire.

- Backup plan for outages. If your internet or power cuts out mid-shift, you need a real fallback — mobile hotspot, secondary ISP, UPS, co-working space, or some combination. You'll describe your specific backup setup in your application.

- Computer: 8 GB RAM minimum (16+ preferred). Processor: Intel Core i5 or equivalent, 8th generation or newer. SSD preferred. Working laptop or desktop

- Mouse

- Wired headset with boom mic (3.5mm or USB-C). No Bluetooth, no laptop mic, no AirPods.

- Webcam — laptop built-in is fine. You'll be on camera for interviews, training, and coaching calls.

- Quiet, dedicated workspace. No roosters, no karaoke neighbors, no babies crying, no traffic, no dogs barking during calls. We will hear it on the call, and so will our clients.



Preferred:



- Second monitor

- You already own a headset that meets the requirements above (we'll provide one if you don't, but having your own helps you start faster)



---



DO NOT APPLY IF:



- You struggle to think quickly and respond in real time. If you need a moment to figure out what to say, this role will be painful. Clients don't wait.

- You need the client to lead the conversation. If you're comfortable answering questions but not steering, this isn't it.

- You can't hold a conversation without a script telling you what to say next.

- You type slowly. Under 40 wpm means you'll fall behind on notes and texts while you're talking.

- You have less than 6 months of experience persuading people, handling objections, and closing toward a booked appointment or sale.

- Your spoken English is hard to understand on the phone — this is a phone role first and the single biggest dealbreaker

- You're juggling multiple clients or planning to freelance on the side. THIS MUST BE YOUR ONLY JOB. We track performance closely and will discover this fast.

- You want a high guaranteed salary with low performance pressure

- You don't like high call volume or you find scripts "suffocating"

- You see remote work as "work whenever you feel like it"

- You can't sustain a graveyard shift long-term

- You're looking for a short-term gig — we expect a minimum 12-month commitment after probation

- STRONG SPOKEN COMMUNICATION — CLEAR, CONFIDENT VOICE. YOU DO NOT RAMBLE. YOU ARE NOT SOFT-SPOKEN. If you fill silence with words because dead air makes you nervous, this won't work.

- Typing speed: 40 wpm minimum (60+ strongly preferred). You'll be taking notes and sending texts while talking. You'll submit a typing test screenshot with your application.

- Process discipline. Every call gets dispositioned correctly. Every lead moves through the right cadence. Every opportunity gets marked accurately in the CRM. This isn't optional admin — it's how we measure everything. Great conversations with sloppy process still means we're flying blind.

- Script discipline for the structured parts of the call.

- Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused.

- Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified.

- Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising.

- Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance.

- CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred.

- High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one.

- Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing.

- Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load.



Preferred:



- Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry

- Personal interest in beauty or self-care

- Experience working with older female clientele (35–65)

- Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster)



Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT):



We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean:



- Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout.

- Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words.

- Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat.

- Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down.

- Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses.

- KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them.



---



TECH REQUIREMENTS



Non-negotiable:



- Internet minimum requirements: 50 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Stable connection. We will test your speed and audio live from your actual work setup before we hire.

- Backup plan for outages. If your internet or power cuts out mid-shift, you need a real fallback — mobile hotspot, secondary ISP, UPS, co-working space, or some combination. You'll describe your specific backup setup in your application.

- Computer: 8 GB RAM minimum (16+ preferred). Processor: Intel Core i5 or equivalent, 8th generation or newer. SSD preferred. Working laptop or desktop

- Mouse

- Wired headset with boom mic (3.5mm or USB-C). No Bluetooth, no laptop mic, no AirPods.

- Webcam — laptop built-in is fine. You'll be on camera for interviews, training, and coaching calls.

- Quiet, dedicated workspace. No roosters, no karaoke neighbors, no babies crying, no traffic, no dogs barking during calls. We will hear it on the call, and so will our clients.



Preferred:



- Second monitor

- You already own a headset that meets the requirements above (we'll provide one if you don't, but having your own helps you start faster)



---



DO NOT APPLY IF:



- You struggle to think quickly and respond in real time. If you need a moment to figure out what to say, this role will be painful. Clients don't wait.

- You need the client to lead the conversation. If you're comfortable answering questions but not steering, this isn't it.

- You can't hold a conversation without a script telling you what to say next.

- You type slowly. Under 40 wpm means you'll fall behind on notes and texts while you're talking.

- You have less than 6 months of experience persuading people, handling objections, and closing toward a booked appointment or sale.

- Your spoken English is hard to understand on the phone — this is a phone role first and the single biggest dealbreaker

- You're juggling multiple clients or planning to freelance on the side. THIS MUST BE YOUR ONLY JOB. We track performance closely and will discover this fast.

- You want a high guaranteed salary with low performance pressure

- You don't like high call volume or you find scripts "suffocating"

- You see remote work as "work whenever you feel like it"

- You can't sustain a graveyard shift long-term

- You're looking for a short-term gig — we expect a minimum 12-month commitment after probation



---



HIRING PROCESS



1. Application via Tally form (link below) — includes voice recording, Loom video, internet speed screenshot, backup plan description, and a few short written questions

2. 20-minute pre-screen call with our hiring partner

3. First-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — includes live roleplay

The role will begin part-time, with an opportunity to increase compensation, responsibilities, and hours as our advertising operation and community grow.

title: Outbound Sales Representative
description:
## About Scalented



Scalented helps businesses **build better teams and scale smarter** by connecting them with high-quality talent tailored to their roles, operations, and company culture.



We work with businesses that need reliable talent without the time, complexity, and cost of managing the entire hiring process themselves.



## The Role



We are looking for a driven **Outbound Sales Representative** to help Scalented acquire new clients.



Your primary responsibility is simple:



**Find businesses that are hiring or could benefit from hiring support, start conversations with the right decision-makers, and turn those conversations into qualified sales opportunities.**



You will focus primarily on outbound prospecting and client acquisition. Scalented will handle the recruitment and service delivery once a client is successfully onboarded.



## What You'll Do



* Identify businesses that may need hiring or staffing support.

* Research and contact founders, business owners, executives, HR leaders, hiring managers, and other decision-makers.

* Conduct outbound outreach through channels such as
, LinkedIn, cold calling, social media, referrals, and networking.

* Introduce Scalented's recruitment and talent solutions.

* Identify each prospect's hiring needs, pain points, and recruitment challenges.

* Qualify potential clients before moving them further into the sales process.

* Schedule discovery or sales calls with qualified prospects.

* Follow up consistently with interested leads.

* Maintain accurate records of prospects, conversations, follow-ups, and outcomes.

* Work with Scalented leadership to improve messaging, targeting, and outbound strategies.

* Help identify industries, niches, and client profiles that respond best to Scalented's services.



## What You'll Be Selling



Scalented provides businesses with recruitment and talent solutions designed around their actual hiring needs.



Depending on the client, this may include:



* Virtual and remote talent

* Specialized professional talent

* Recruitment support

* Candidate sourcing and screening

* Talent matching based on role requirements and company fit

* Customized hiring solutions for growing businesses



You do **not** need to recruit or source candidates yourself.



Your responsibility is to **bring qualified businesses to Scalented.**



## Ideal Candidate



You may be a strong fit if you:



* Have experience in outbound sales, business development, lead generation, appointment setting, recruitment sales, staffing sales, or B2B sales.

* Are comfortable reaching out to people who have never heard of Scalented.

* Can communicate confidently with business owners and senior decision-makers.

* Know how to research companies and identify genuine business opportunities.

* Understand that successful outbound sales requires consistent follow-up.

* Are comfortable working independently and managing your own pipeline.

* Are motivated by performance-based compensation.

* Can represent Scalented professionally in written and verbal communication.



Experience selling **recruitment, staffing, HR, outsourcing, virtual assistant, professional services, or other B2B services** is highly desirable but not required.



## How You'll Be Measured



Performance will primarily be evaluated based on:



* Qualified opportunities generated

* Sales meetings booked

* Meeting attendance/show rate

* Qualified proposals or opportunities created

* New clients acquired

* Revenue generated



We care more about **real business generated than activity for activity's sake.**



Sending thousands of generic messages is not the goal. Creating conversations with businesses that genuinely need Scalented is.



## What Scalented Provides



Scalented will provide:



* Company and service information

* Ideal client profiles

* Sales positioning and messaging

* Outreach templates and talking points

* Sales collateral

* Guidance on qualifying opportunities

* Support during discovery and closing when needed

* Recruitment and service delivery once the client signs



Your job is to **open doors and create revenue opportunities.**



## Why Scalented?



We're building a talent business around a straightforward idea:



**Better Talent for Better Businesses.**



Instead of selling generic candidate lists, Scalented aims to understand what a business actually needs and connect it with people who can help it grow.



If you're good at finding opportunities, starting conversations, and turning cold prospects into real business relationships, we'd like to work with you.



**Build Better. Scale Smarter.**

title: Senior Software Architect / Technical Lead (AI-Native)
description:
Senior Software Architect / Technical Lead (AI-Native)



Remote | Full-Time | $25 USD/hour | 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM EST



I’m looking for a Senior Software Architect / Technical Lead to join me in building and scaling a modern software platform for property management companies.



This is a hands-on technical leadership role. I’m not looking for someone who simply manages developers or spends most of their time in meetings. I want a strong engineer who can think architecturally, write excellent code, solve difficult technical problems, and lead a development team while moving quickly.



We’re building software and AI-powered automations that handle complex property management workflows, so the work involves real-world integrations, automation, data synchronization, multi-tenant architecture, and plenty of interesting edge cases.



What You’ll Do

Architect & Build

Own the technical architecture for scalable, multi-tenant SaaS applications.

Design systems that support both standardized workflows and client-specific customization.

Make thoughtful architectural decisions without overengineering.

Build prototypes and turn ideas into production-ready solutions.

Build Complex Integrations

Design and maintain integrations with property management platforms such as Rent Manager, AppFolio, Yardi, and Buildium.

Work with APIs, webhooks, authentication systems, data synchronization, and third-party services.

Develop reliable strategies for handling inconsistent or incomplete external data.

Automation & AI

Design resilient web scraping and browser automation systems when native APIs aren't available.

Leverage modern AI development tools to dramatically accelerate development.

Use Claude, Claude Code, AI agents, and AI-powered IDEs as part of your everyday engineering workflow.

Know when to trust AI-generated code—and, more importantly, when to challenge, test, refactor, or reject it.

Stay Hands-On

Write production code.

Debug complex issues.

Review pull requests.

Identify and resolve technical bottlenecks.

Improve testing, monitoring, reliability, and production performance.

Be willing to jump into the codebase rather than simply delegate.

Lead & Mentor

Provide technical direction to other developers.

Establish and maintain strong engineering standards.

Review architecture and code for quality, security, and maintainability.

Help the team move quickly without sacrificing long-term stability.

Work Directly With Me



I’m looking for someone who can take ambitious product ideas and turn them into simple, practical technical solutions.



You should be comfortable pushing back when you believe there’s a better or simpler approach. I value engineers who can say, “There’s a much easier way to build this,” and then explain why.



What I’m Looking For



Strong technical experience with:



TypeScript / JavaScript

Node.js

React / Next.js

Python

PostgreSQL

Modern cloud infrastructure

Automated testing

Monitoring and observability

Production debugging



You should also have experience with:



Multi-tenant SaaS architecture

Third-party API integrations

Web scraping and browser automation

Authentication and authorization systems

Data synchronization and event-driven workflows

Designing systems for reliability and scale

You’re the Kind of Engineer I Want If…

You’re a senior-level engineer who still loves writing code.

You naturally think about edge cases, failure modes, permissions, security, and data integrity.

You’ve worked with systems involving sensitive business or financial information.

You can look at a complicated requirement and find the simplest architecture that solves it properly.

You’re comfortable working independently and making technical decisions.

You move quickly but don’t cut corners that will create bigger problems later.

You enjoy mentoring developers and raising the technical bar.

You already use AI extensively in your development workflow.

You understand that AI can make you dramatically faster—but engineering judgment is still essential.

AI-Native Engineering Is Important



I’m specifically looking for someone who has embraced the new generation of AI-assisted development.



You should be comfortable using tools like Claude and Claude Code to:



Explore unfamiliar codebases

Generate and refactor code

Build prototypes quickly

Debug issues

Automate repetitive engineering tasks

Work with AI agents



But this isn’t about blindly accepting AI-generated code. You need enough technical depth to audit AI output, identify security and architectural problems, test thoroughly, and maintain high engineering standards.



Work Schedule & Compensation



Position: Senior Software Architect / Technical Lead

Employment: Full-Time

Schedule: 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM EST, Monday–Friday

Hours: 40 hours/week

Rate: $25 USD/hour (~$4,000/month)

description:
Client Background

Our client is a Los Angeles–based creator-powered media company and TikTok Shop agency specializing in high-volume, founder-led short-form content across TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, LinkedIn, and
.

The team operates within clearly defined content lanes, where each editor owns a specific lane and works efficiently using established templates, brand presets, and references, allowing for speed and consistency without reinventing the wheel for every piece.



Their tech stack includes Descript, Adobe Premiere, CapCut, Notion, and Claude.

They are currently hiring for three roles. Across all positions, they value individuals who are reliable, coachable, and proactive in owning well-defined responsibilities. The roles are intentionally structured to help team members perform at their best, balancing speed, storytelling, and sound judgment where each matters most.





Role Title: Video Editor - Volume Lane 



High-throughput short-form editor who owns one content lane and produces clean, on-brand cuts fast, to a template. 





Primary Goal 

Turn raw footage, talking-head, creator calls, simple scripted pieces, into polished short-form videos at high volume, following established templates, brand presets, and references. Success is measured by consistent daily output at a reliable quality bar, not by creative reinvention. 



Where This Role Sits 

You are assigned one primary content lane (for example: scripted talking-head, reply-to-comment clips, or creator-call highlight clips). A producer hands you organized footage, a template, and a reference; you execute. This is a focused, repeatable role for someone who likes to get into flow and ship. 





Key Responsibilities 

• Edit raw footage into finished short-form videos (TikTok, Reels, Shorts) using provided templates and brand presets. 

• Apply captions, basic text overlays, clean cuts, and audio cleanup to a consistent standard. 

• Hit a daily output target without dropping below the quality floor. 

• Multiply each approved cut into platform-native variants,  turning one finished piece into several posts across TikTok, Reels, Shorts, LinkedIn, and
 (aspect ratio, length, caption style). 

• Keep project files, exports, and assets organized and named per our system. 

• Use AI tools (Claude, OpusClip, 
) to speed up culling, rough cuts, and reformatting. 





Required Skills & Tools 

• Core editing: Descript and/or CapCut (required); Adobe Premiere a plus. 

• Captioning workflows and platform-native formatting for TikTok / Reels / Shorts. 

• AI-assisted editing: OpusClip, 
; comfortable working alongside Claude. 

• Collaboration: Google Workspace, Slack / Lark, Loom. 





Experience 

1–2+ years editing short-form social content. Hungry, fast-learning editors early in their career are welcome, we would rather build good habits than undo bad ones. 







What We Screen For 

• Speed with consistency: a high volume of clean edits per day, every day, to a template. 

• Lane discipline and coachability: thrives inside a defined system; does not need creative control or to make the content their own. 

• Reliability: predictable daily throughput we can build a pipeline around. 





Not a fit if: you want a creative-director track, heavy input on concept/strategy, or get restless doing the same content type repeatedly. That is a different role, see Story / Hero Editor.

title: Marketing Strategist
description:
We’re Looking for a Marketing Strategist — Not Just Another Marketer



Are you the kind of marketer who doesn’t just ask, “What should we post?”



But instead asks:



- “Is our marketing actually working?”

- “Where are we getting ROI?”

- “What should we stop doing?”

- “Where should we invest more?”



If that sounds like you, we want to hear from you.



We’re a U.S.-based organization, the American Academy of Estate Planning Attorneys (AAEPA), helping attorneys grow their law firms through membership, training, and strategic education.



We’re hiring a Fractional Marketing Strategist who can think like an operator and strategist — not just an executor.



This is NOT a role where we simply hand you a list of tasks and ask you to execute.



We need someone who can look at our entire marketing ecosystem, identify opportunities, dig into the numbers, and confidently tell us:



What’s working.



What isn’t.



Why.



And what we should do next.



What you’ll be doing:



- Audit our current marketing efforts and determine what is actually producing results.

- Build and monitor tracking so we can confidently measure campaign performance and ROI.

- Recommend where we should invest, reduce, or reallocate our marketing budget.

- Analyze our CRM, contact database, lifecycle stages, funnels, and attribution.

- Identify opportunities for growth and improvement.

- Develop a focused 30/60/90-day marketing plan centered on high-impact activities.



What we’re looking for:



- You have proven B2B marketing experience, preferably in businesses with longer sales cycles.

- You’re comfortable looking at metrics, ROI, conversion rates, attribution, and budgets.

- You understand CRMs, funnels,
 marketing, automation, and analytics.

- You can work independently, prioritize ruthlessly, and make smart decisions with limited hours.

- And most importantly, you have excellent written English and strong communication skills.



⭐ Bonus points if you’ve worked with membership organizations, professional associations, coaching, training, education, or similar business models.



This opportunity may be a great fit if…



- You enjoy figuring things out.

- You don't need someone telling you what to do every hour.

- You’re comfortable saying, “I don’t think this is working, and here’s why.”

- You know how to turn data into decisions.

- And you’re excited by the idea of having a meaningful impact on a growing organization.

- We’re looking for someone who can own the strategy — not just complete the checklist.



If that sounds like you, we’d love to meet you.



or if you know someone who would be an excellent fit, feel free to tag them or share this post.

We're a marketing agency for industrial manufacturers and B2B companies. We're looking for an organized, detail-oriented Web Project & Operations Manager to oversee WordPress projects, coordinate with our developer, do QA, and handle website-related client communication. Not a dev role — we already have a strong developer. We need someone who keeps things moving and catches details.



Important: This role is meant to grow into full-time. We need someone who can treat this as their primary job, not a side gig.



Requirements

Prior experience as a Project Manager directly managing a developer (not just using PM tools)

The scope pushback: A client insists on a change that your developer says is a bad idea technically (e.g., will break mobile responsiveness or slow the site down). The client won't budge. What do you actually do — and what do you say to each side?

title: Influencer Outreach & Partnerships Manager – Luxury Fashion Brand
description:
HOLT, a luxury women's fashion brand specializing in statement pieces handmade in Miami, is looking for a highly motivated **Influencer Outreach & Partnerships Manager** to aggressively grow our influencer, celebrity, stylist, and creator network.



This is primarily an **OUTREACH position**.



We are looking for someone who can spend every day discovering the right influencers, contacting them, following up, negotiating collaborations, coordinating gifting, and building long-term relationships that generate exposure, content, traffic, and sales for HOLT.



## Your Main Responsibility



**Get HOLT into the hands of the right women and get HOLT seen.**

* Fashion influencers

* Luxury lifestyle influencers

* Miami influencers

* New York and Los Angeles influencers

* Resort and travel creators

* Celebrity stylists

* Fashion stylists

* Models and personalities

* Reality-TV personalities

* Content creators and UGC creators

* Fashion editors and other relevant industry contacts



## Responsibilities

s, management information, agencies, and other contact methods

* Invite influencers to HOLT events, launches, pop-ups, shoots, and other activations

* Identify opportunities for celebrity and stylist placements

* Track discount codes, affiliate links, traffic, engagement, and sales when applicable

* Maintain an organized influencer CRM/database

* Keep detailed records of every contact, response, product sent, collaboration, post, and result

* Report results weekly



## Daily Outreach Expectations



This is a proactive position. We do not want someone waiting for influencers to contact us.



You should be comfortable maintaining a consistent daily pipeline of **new outreach + follow-ups + active collaborations**.



Quality matters. We are not interested in randomly messaging thousands of accounts. Every influencer should be evaluated for:



**Brand Fit + Audience + Engagement + Location + Content Quality + Sales Potential**



## What Success Looks Like



We will measure:



**Qualified Influencers Contacted → Responses → Products Requested → Collaborations Confirmed → Products Sent → Content Posted → Reach/Engagement → Website Traffic → Sales**



The goal isn't simply to send free clothing.



The goal is to turn influencer outreach into **brand awareness, beautiful content, relationships, and revenue.**



## Ideal Candidate



You should:



* Understand Instagram and TikTok extremely well

* Have excellent written English

* Be comfortable sending large amounts of personalized outreach

* Be persistent with follow-ups

* Have a strong eye for fashion and aesthetics

* Understand luxury positioning

* Know the difference between follower count and real influence

* Be able to evaluate engagement and audience quality

* Be extremely organized

* Communicate professionally with influencers, managers, and stylists

* Understand gifting and influencer collaborations

* Be comfortable negotiating

* Work independently

* Be highly responsive

* Be motivated by measurable results



Previous experience with **fashion, beauty, luxury, influencer marketing, PR, celebrity placement, or creator partnerships** is strongly preferred.



## Tools



Experience with any of the following is helpful:



Instagram • TikTok • Shopify • Canva • Google Sheets • Influencer databases • CRM platforms • Affiliate platforms • ChatGPT/AI tools



## To Apply



Please send:



1. Your resume

2. Your previous influencer-marketing experience

3. Fashion, beauty, or luxury brands you have worked with

4. Examples of influencer campaigns you have managed

5. Your expected monthly salary

6. Your availability and time zone

**1 Instagram DM** you would send to an influencer you want to gift HOLT.



**1
** you would send to an influencer's manager proposing a collaboration.



We are looking for someone who can become the person responsible for **building HOLT's influencer network from the ground up and turning relationships into meaningful exposure and sales.**

title: Website Optimization Project - React/Lovable Site, CRO + Technical SEO (project, then ongoing)
description:
INTRO: 



We have a live e-commerce website for a US health and wellness brand. It was built quickly using AI tools and it works, but it has never been properly audited, optimized or tuned for conversion. We want someone to go through it end to end, tell us what's wrong, and then fix it.



This starts as a paid fixed-scope project of roughly 4-6 weeks. If it goes well, and we'd like it to, it becomes an ongoing monthly retainer of 10-15 hours per week, working alongside our marketing lead on landing pages and A/B tests. We are looking for a long-term working relationship, not a one-and-done.



ABOUT:



Pep'd is a US-based health and wellness company selling directly to consumers through a telehealth subscription model. Small team, founder-led, fast decisions. You'll work with the founder directly.



Phase 1 - the project



Deliverable 1: Conversion tracking



Audit and fix all conversion tracking: Meta Pixel, Conversions API, GA4 events, any other pixels

Verify that every event fires once, fires accurately, and matches actual purchases

Set up Google Search Console and confirm the site is being indexed correctly

This is the highest priority item. Our ad spend is worthless without it.



Deliverable 2: Written audit



A prioritized document of everything wrong or suboptimal on the site

Each item scored by estimated impact and effort, so we can d
 what to fix

Cover: performance, mobile experience, checkout and funnel friction, broken elements, accessibility, technical SEO

Include Lighthouse / PageSpeed scores as a baseline



Deliverable 3: Performance and mobile



Fix Core Web Vitals: LCP, CLS, INP

Image optimization, lazy loading, bundle size, render-blocking resources

Full mobile responsiveness pass on real devices, not just a browser resize

Target: measurable, documented before/after scores



Deliverable 4: Conversion path



Find and remove friction in the path from landing to purchase

Form validation, error states, loading states, trust signals, clear calls to action

Fix anything broken: dead links, 404s, forms that fail silently, layout breaks



Deliverable 5: Technical SEO foundation



XML sitemap, robots.txt, canonical tags

Title tags and meta descriptions across all pages

Correct heading hierarchy (one H1 per page, logical structure)

Schema markup: Organization, Product, FAQ, Breadcrumb

Fix crawl errors, redirect chains, duplicate content issues

Note: this role covers TECHNICAL SEO only. Keyword research and content writing are handled by our marketing lead.



Deliverable 6: Handover



Short written summary of what changed and why

A prioritized list of what you'd do next if we continue



Phase 2 — the retainer (if we both want it)



Build and ship new landing pages for marketing campaigns

Set up and run A/B tests, report on results

Ongoing maintenance, monitoring and speed upkeep

Implement technical SEO recommendations as the content program grows

10-15 hours per week, paid monthly



Requirements



Strong React / TypeScript. Our site is built on a modern React stack (Lovable-generated codebase). You must be comfortable working with an existing codebase you did not write.

Experience with AI-generated codebases and cleaning them up

Demonstrable CRO experience - you have improved a real site's conversion rate and can show the numbers

Technical SEO experience with hands-on Search Console work

Experience implementing and debugging Meta Pixel, Conversions API and GA4

Comfortable with Git, staging environments and deploying safely

Good written English. The audit document has to be readable by a non-technical founder.

Available for at least 2-3 hours of overlap with US Eastern Time (marketing lead will be on similar time zone to you).



Nice to have



E-commerce or DTC experience

Health, wellness or supplement industry experience

A/B testing tools (PostHog, VWO, Google Optimize alternatives)





SALARY 



$3-$7 / hour with hours tracked 

selected applicant will submit a rough estimate for each stage of the project ( Number of hours required)

Before submitting your application, please visit our website:
